findings.summary: Medium::seek never checks the cancel token in the SeekMode::Keyframe path (nor on the empty-index return): a cancelled seek returns Ok instead of Err(Cancelled). Probe P10.
The fraction steps by done/planned with planned = duration x fps; when the packet count differs, the last report jumps and the 0.02 step bound of ARQ-139 breaks. Probe P17.
KeyframeIndex::build keeps the keyframe times in the order the container gave them and never sorts them, although the type documents them as ascending; the binary search then lands wrong.
The implementer edited crates/gafira-testkit/Cargo.toml, a single-writer file of SC1, to add gafira-time to the ports feature; the default graph does not change, so V5, ARQ-107 and deny stay green.
ARQ-138, a Product ID of the card, is proved in substance by the clippy gate and by an ARQ-144-named test, but no test names ARQ-138: git grep ARQ-138 reaches only a module header.
The delivery is 1401 code lines against a ceiling of ~700 and an adjusted forecast of 600: twice the ceiling, outside the x1.4-x1.9 band. It needs the explicit OK of the owner.
XP6, the claim of the <=1 s per minute of 1080p material that the design marks as blocking ME1, was never measured: no spike exists and the crate ships no bench for the scan.
